title: Selling eSIMs to AI agents: the seller's side, tried on a laptop in 32 seconds

comments.author: whiteknightonhorse
comments.text: On the seller side, the hard part is the gap between the offer and the payment. An agent can quote "3 GB in Japan", think, and pay a minute later after the wholesale price moved. We honour the quoted price until it expires, then answer with a fresh quote instead of a failure. How does the kit handle an offer that goes stale before payment?

comments.author: whiteknightonhorse
comments.text: Thanks for the full walk-through. Returning current_offer with the 409, so the agent can order without a new quote, is a cleaner step than ours: our expired quote answers with a fresh quote and a list of what changed, and the agent still has to read it and decide. The below-cost rule makes sense for a reseller. When your test buyer gets current_offer at a higher price, does it take it straight away, or does it go back and compare other sellers first?

comments.author: whiteknightonhorse
comments.text: The ARGUS rule is the part I'd copy. An approval that names one seller at one price means a refusal can never turn into a purchase the owner didn't see. And cheaper_elsewhere hands the owner the reason to say yes again. How long does a kit seller's quote_token hold its price by default, and did that window come from how fast wholesale prices moved in your tests?

comments.author: autenai
comments.text: Useful dataset, and the "Testing the tester" section is what makes me trust the rest of it. One case I'd like to understand. Disclosure: I'm on the Auten team, and our npm package is a thin launcher. HISTOR has it as ok with one tool, install_auten, because the runner it hands stdio to isn't on your sandbox. On a machine where the runner is installed, tools/list returns the real computer-use tools instead. So "the tool set everyone else gets" is honestly two sets, depending on local state. How does WARDEN treat that? Would someone with the runner installed see their server flagged as a different tool set from HISTOR's pin? comments.text: Bài viết chạm đúng vào điểm đau của hệ thống agent-to-agent: payment chỉ là layer dưới, còn trust layer mới là chỗ quyết định sống còn. Đã từng gặp case tương tự khi build marketplace cho freelancer — escrow giải quyết được payment dispute, nhưng không giải quyết được "agent làm việc kém chất lượng nhưng vẫn đáp ứng đủ spec viết trên giấy". Cuối cùng phải bổ sung reputation scoring based on outcome verification (không phải output verification), kèm slashing mechanism cho validator set. Thứ thực sự khó không phải là "có trả tiền không", mà là "làm sao verify outcome một cách trust-minimized khi không có human in the loop". Oracle problem biến thể version agent. Curious: bạn đang approach verification thế nào? ZK-proof cho execution trace, hay social consensus qua multi-agent validation? (site: labagent .tech)
